key_insight: A Video Vision Transformer can learn to predict the full time evolution of viscoelastic droplet impacts from only the first 10%–20% of a simulation, cutting cost while preserving key physics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster surrogate for droplet-impact design in spray cooling, inkjet printing, and pharma processing where many parameter sweeps are otherwise expensive.
method: Input early-time VOF volume-fraction fields from viscoelastic droplet impact simulations.
Train a ViViT model to forecast the remaining temporal evolution of the droplet.
Use predictions across different regimes and horizons, including spreading and bouncing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports physically consistent predictions across parameter settings and horizons, with about 80%–90% reduction in computational cost versus full simulation.
watch_item: The approach is only as reliable as the training coverage of impact regimes and may need careful validation before using experimental video data or extrapolating to unseen fluid parameters.
paper_title: Prediction of Viscoelastic Droplet Impact Dynamics Using a Vision Transformer-Based Approach
